To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zircon size is correlated with host sand size and that this correlation implies hydrodynamic fractionation.

(i) zircon size is correlated with host sand size; (ii) zircon size varies with age; (iii) different zircon age populations are hy- drodynamically distinct; (iv) different hydrodynamic microenvironments of a dune present different detrital age spectra; (v) the age spectra of samples from the same hydrodynamic microenvironment are not identical; and (vi) hydrodynamic fractionation occurs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how much of the detrital zircons in the Amazon River are derived from the Amazonian Shield?
the question of whether or not the age distribution of detrital zircons can be used to reconstruct sediment provenance.
the question of how detrital zircons are transported and deposited in rivers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hydrodynamic fractiona- tion of zircon age population does occur.
the hydrodynamic fractionation does occur, and it can be observed, but it is not the only factor controlling the detrital zircons size.
the size of the zircons in the samples is controlled by the hydraulic conditions of the river.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
zircon age populations are not hydrau- lically equivalent and are not hydraulically blind to host sand size.
hydrodynamic fractiona- tion of zircon age distributions is a real effect, but that it is not a major effect in most cases.
hydrodynamic fraction- ation is an important process in detrital- zircon studies, and that it should be con- sidered in all studies of detrital zircons, and in all studies of zircons in general.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zircon size should be considered when interpreting the provenance of detrital zircons in sediments.
zircon size is a proxy for zircon provenance and that zir- con size is correlated with host sand size.
the zircon size distribution in a sample can provide information about the transport history of the zircons.
